newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forwards tumble.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forwards tumble.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady at 35.8175/8200 against the dollar in the spot market but continued its gains against the forward dollar on Monday, dealers said.
The spot rupee moved in the 35.50/8175 band in dull trade throughout the day, dealers said. No one expected much demand as month-end demand was exhausted on the weekend, they said.
The State Bank of India (SBI), India's leading bank, was not very active on Monday but bought dollars from some banks which approached it, they said.
A foreign bank bought dollars at the 35.82 level towards the close of trade on Monday, they said.
Forward dollar premiums continued to tumble, braked by profit-taking during the day, dealers said.
"It looked like going up for a while, but didn't," the chief dealer at a Bombay bank said.
The six-month annualised premium closed at 3.23 percent compared with Friday's close of 3.46 percent, he said.
The chief dealer at a state-run bank said this was the right level. "Premiums should be in the 3.25-4.0 percent band, taking into account the interest differentials," he said.
